text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Paging: latency_slo_breach detected on /stream/v1 (p99) — escalated to oncall. Incident ID: INC-2026-0912

Maria Velasquez: I’m on it, grabbing oncall. p95 jumped ~4x across the last 10m, streaming stalls reported.

Aj Patel: Ack, picking up (oncall). Seeing p95 ~450ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~1.8s on the streaming tier. Customers with long sessions hit most.

Devon Li: Context: CPU endpoints look fine, this seems isolated to GPU-backed streaming pods in cluster us-west-2-a.

Tess Huang: Any related deploys in the last 30m?

Aj Patel: No deploys. Deploy bot shows last deploy 2h ago.

Incident Bot: Related alert: streaming_tail_stall (count 97), node_metric_gpu_ecc_correctable (node=gpu-node-12)

Maria Velasquez: @Aj can you confirm which nodes are seeing ECC / thermal messages?

Aj Patel: Quick grep on logs — node gpu-node-12 shows repeated correctable ECC and thermal throttle messages. Example from dmesg: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00:0): 13, CE single-bit error at address 0x7ff...` and `thermal警告: GPU 0 reduced clock`

Devon Li: I’m pulling nvml metrics now. nvml shows repeated `CE` counters incrementing and temperature spikes to 92C before throttle.

Ops Runner: Rolling mitigation plan: 1) divert new streaming sessions away from affected pool, 2) drain affected node, 3) fallback to CPU streaming cluster for active sessions longer than 30s where possible.

Aj Patel: Starting traffic shift to fallback route (policy: prefer-cpu when node in degraded). Will reduce concurrency on GPU pool to avoid stalls.

Tess Huang: Customer Success — which customers are impacted? I can proactively notify.

Customer Success: We have 3 paid customers with high usage hitting errors/latency: acme-corp, echohealth, and big-retailer. Already seeing support tickets for “stream stalls / slow responses”.

Aj Patel: Executing `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -l platform=streaming`

Maria Velasquez: Paste the exact command so we can audit in the incident log.

Aj Patel:

```kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -l app=streaming-worker --force
```

Devon Li: Adding a temporary policy: reduce batch_size by 50% on streaming workers to reduce per-request latency variance. Pushing config via rollout: `cfg/streaming/batch_reduction=true`

Incident Bot: oncall handoff scheduled in 25m from Aj -> Devon if still active.

Ops Runner: Observability note: enabling extended KV prefix caching for popular prefixes to reduce repeated token computation. Might help p95 but not p99 hardware stalls.

Aj Patel: I see kube drains in progress, pods coming up in other AZs (us-west-2-b). Real-time metrics: p95 trending down to ~600ms after routing, p99 still ~1.1s due to a handful of long tails.

Devon Li: Can we snapshot the node for hardware debug before we power cycle? Need kernel logs + nvidia-smi -q output.

Aj Patel: Collected nvml logs and uploaded to S3: https://internal-s3/redwood/incidents/1759999991/nvml.log

Maria Velasquez: Good. Please also tag the ticket with potential hardware (ECC/thermal) so HW-ops can open an RMA if needed.

Customer Success: We posted a short notice to affected customers: “We’re aware of increased latency for streaming sessions in US-West, working on mitigation. We’ll follow up with timeline.”

Tess Huang: Any immediate customer-facing mitigation? Can we force-fallback big-retailer to a dedicated CPU route as a stopgap?

Aj Patel: Yes, I can emergency route big-retailer to the reserved CPU pool for the next 2 hours. Doing now.

Devon Li: After drain completes, we should run `nvidia-bug-report` and capture ECC counters. Also plan to isolate PCIe slot to rule out riser issues.

Ops Runner: Thermal mitigation: schedule node power cycle and BIOS fan profile bump. But need on-call approval — power cycle will evict workloads briefly.

Aj Patel: Approved for power cycle after snapshot. Will coordinate with HW-ops.

Incident Bot: Action logged — mitigation: routed 3 customers to CPU fallback, drained node gpu-node-12, reduced batch size, enabled prefix caching.

Maria Velasquez: Customer Success — please update customers with ETA ~30-45m, mention we have a mitigation in place and are doing hardware triage.

Customer Success: Sent update.

Devon Li: Monitoring: p95 now ~320ms, p99 ~450ms, streaming stall count down from 97 -> 3 in last 10m. Looks stable but we'll keep node out of rotation for 2h for postmortem.

Tess Huang: Assigning postmortem to Devon + Aj. Please include timeline, root cause hypothesis (ECC + thermal causing throttles), and action items (RMA, BIOS fan tuning, telemetry improvements).

Aj Patel: Handing oncall to Devon early — I need to step off for a meeting. Leaving notes in the incident doc.

Devon Li: Taking over oncall. Thanks @Aj. I’ll own the remainder of the live mitigation and the postmortem.

Maria Velasquez: Thanks team. After action items: (1) Improve early signal for CE bursts -> trigger preemptive traffic shift, (2) add node-level thermal SLO alert lower threshold, (3) test fallback path weekly.

Incident Bot: Incident INC-2026-0912 marked as mitigation in-progress. Next update required in 30m or on significant state change.

Customer Success: Customers acknowledged, one asks for a follow-up once full resolution — scheduling a follow-up email.

Devon Li: Closing thread when node is either returned to service with hardware cleared or RMA done. Current plan: keep node quarantined until ECC counters stable for 2 hours after reboot.

Aj Patel: Quick note for the record: observed `nvme` errors concurrently on that rack (maybe unrelated) — pinging infra to check rack-level power/cooling.

Ops Runner: Infra alerted: Checking rack cooling logs and PDUs. Will update.

Maria Velasquez: Great. If anything regresses, re-pager immediately. Otherwise, we’ll capture full timeline and root cause for the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
